label: Kodak T-Max 400
source: Kodak Alaris Inc., KODAK PROFESSIONAL T-MAX 400 Film technical data, KODAK Publication No. F-4043 (February 2016); curves read from the PDF's vector chart paths (pages 7 and 8)
notes: Approximate digitization; not supplied or endorsed by Kodak Alaris Inc. or Eastman Kodak Company. The page-8 characteristic curves and the page-7 spectral-sensitivity curves are vector paths in the PDF; curve vertices were read directly from the path geometry (no raster tracing; the solid curves' Bezier segments were sampled at 8 steps) and axes calibrated on the vector frame and tick marks (log H -4.0..+1.0, density 0..4.0; 250-750 nm on the vector grid lines, log sensitivity 0..4.0), then resampled linearly on a 0.02 log H grid and a 1 nm grid. Characteristic curves (page 8, 'Exposure: Daylight; Densitometry: Diffuse Visual'): three charts, KODAK PROFESSIONAL Developer D-76 small tank 20 C (68 F) 6/8/11 min, KODAK PROFESSIONAL T-MAX Developer small tank 24 C (75 F) 5/7/9 min, and KODAK PROFESSIONAL T-MAX RS Developer and Replenisher large tank 24 C (75 F) 5/7/9 min; all nine are in all_curves. Curves were matched to their time labels by line style (solid, long dash, short dash as labelled) and checked by density order at log H -1.0 (longer time, higher density). channels.k is T-MAX RS Developer and Replenisher, large tank, 24 C (75 F), 5 min: the processing starting points (page 3) are 'intended to produce negatives with a contrast appropriate for printing with a diffusion enlarger', and the large-tank rolls table gives T-MAX RS at 75 F for 5 min, which is the only charted curve that equals a recommended starting-point time and temperature (the small-tank starting points are D-76 68 F 7 1/2 min, between the charted 6 and 8 min, and T-MAX 75 F 5 1/2 min, between the charted 5 and 7 min). All curves begin at log H -3.5 and end near log H +0.34 as charted. x is log H (lux-seconds) as charted. log_h_ref: none. The charts carry no 18% grey, speed-point or normal-exposure mark, so no reference exposure is placed; the text gives ISO 400/27. Spectral sensitivity (page 7): 'LOG SENSITIVITY', sensitivity = reciprocal of exposure (erg/cm2) required to produce specified density; Process: KODAK PROFESSIONAL Developer D-76, 20 C (68 F); Densitometry: Diffuse Visual. Two curves are charted, D = 0.3 and D = 1.0 greater than D-min; channels.k is the D = 1.0 curve (mid-tone level), and both are kept in spectral_sensitivity.all_curves. The D = 0.3 curve ends in a near-vertical drop at about 650 nm, kept as charted. rms_granularity is the printed diffuse rms granularity 10 (image structure based on D-76 at 68 F (20 C); read at a net diffuse density of 1.00, 48 um aperture, 12x); no granularity curve is published. Not recorded (no field in this schema): contrast-index vs development-time curves (page 8), MTF curve (page 7), resolving power (50 lines/mm at TOC 1.6:1, 200 lines/mm at 1000:1), development-time adjustment factors, reciprocity and push-processing tables.
